A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a baseline for the usage of gesture effects in human-to-human communication.
we have provided a set of gesture type guidelines which are suitable for the design of gesture interfaces for interactive environments, surfaces, and displays.

we present a study that shows the preferences for usage of gesture types for directing other humans, in a way that can be used as a baseline to design gesture driven interfaces for HCI, and as guidelines for designing new gesture languages for interactive systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are preferences for gesture types, and these preferences should be taken into account in designing gesture languages for HCI.
the design of gesture languages should be informed by a thorough understanding of the gesture types used by humans.
